findings.problem: The nonresident-alien row states 'FICA on actual wages, as for residents' with no exemption. Pub. 515 (2026), registered as US-FEDS5-016 with a local copy, says F-1, J-1, M-1 and Q nonimmigrants are exempt from social security and Medicare on qualifying wages (IRC 3121(b)(19)), and that totalization agreements can exempt inbound workers who hold a certificate of coverage. The CCG has no totalization content anywhere (0 hits), and the 6.0 matrix covers income tax only. The v2.12 C31 logic returns MANUAL because there is no non-resident social-security sentence.
findings.expected: Facts for the NRA FICA/FUTA exemptions (3121(b)(19) classes and their limits; totalization certificate of coverage and the SSA agreement list) from Pub. 515 and SSA primary pages; the m05 row corrected; a FICA/FUTA column added to the 6.0 resident vs non-resident matrix; a cross-reference in annex_FED.

findings.problem: F44 local re-verification: 79 numeric keys the CCG consumes have a value that is NOT in the local copy of their cited register row but IS in the local copy of another row. Examples: sc.pit.wh.band.* and sc.pit.oracle.example_1.withholding cite US-SCS5-004 (WH-1603 wage-bracket tables), while 3,640 / 18,230 / 109.20 / 656.10 / 10.58 are in WH-1603F (US-SCP51-002 / US-SC-007); ct.oracle.ex8/9/10 (17.65 / 39.97 / 78.82) cite TPG-211 (US-CTS5-010) but are in IP 2026(1) (US-CTP10-001); wa.pfml.total.rate 2026 cites US-WAS5-011 (RCW 50A.10, which carries no rate) in the annex_WA facts and US-WAS5-015 in the m05 and WTC facts. The values are right, but the cited row does not carry the figure (separation rule #5).
findings.expected: Re-point the register_id of each listed key to the row whose instrument carries the figure, with one row per fact across the CCG and WTC facts, then re-render the CCG citations.

findings.problem: The F44 target (100 % local re-verification) was not reached. Of the 2,016 numeric keys the CCG tags, 1,818 were confirmed against local copies: 1,639 directly in the cited row's file, 152 in another row's file, and 27 by QA re-derivation or manual reading. 198 could not be confirmed: 59 entries sit on rows with no local_file (e.g. fed.fica.oasdi.wage_base 2027 = 192,300 on US-FED-022; pa.sui.* on US-PA-009; nc.pit.nra.addon.* on US-NC-001); 74 are statute values written in words or held in font-encoded PDFs (the Pittsburgh PSDA PDF has no usable text layer); 71 are small integers found only out of context; the rest are derived values that were not reproduced.
findings.expected: A local copy (with md5) for every row a CCG number rests on, and a text or OCR copy for font-encoded PDFs, so that 0 numeric keys remain unverified.

findings.location: 01-ccg/US-CCG-001-v1.0.docx!Annex CT CT.1 and Annex DE DE.10!table 301 r2c6; table 332 r3c5
findings.problem: Value matching has created wrong fact bindings. In CT, 'headcount for week containing [[FACT:ct.leave.sick.coverage_threshold_employees=1]] Jan' binds the date '1 Jan' to the 2027 sick-leave threshold. In DE, 'penalties 1,000-[[FACT:de.pit.bracket.2.ceiling=5,000]] + treble' binds a prevailing-wage penalty to the PIT bracket ceiling. A future change to either fact would silently rewrite unrelated text when the CCG is regenerated, and C46 counts both as valid bindings.
findings.expected: '1 January' untagged; the DE penalty range tagged to its own penalty fact (or left untagged with its register id). Audit the generators' value-matching tagger for the same pattern.
